title: Beyond Softmax and Entropy: Convergence Rates of Policy Gradients with $\boldsymbol{f}$-SoftArgmax Parameterization $\&$ Coupled Regularization
claim: The standard parameterization and regularizer create flat, vanishing-gradient regions; our coupled alternative gives a smooth landscape that optimization can traverse.
layout: 2 side-by-side 3D surface plots, left-to-right, shared viridis color scale
description: Two 3D surface plots of a regularized value landscape for a one-state, two-action MDP, shown side by side. The axes are the policy parameters, with theta_1 labeled and tick values from -30 to 30. The left surface is the softmax with entropy. It is a nearly vertical cliff between a large flat purple plateau at the bottom and a flat yellow-green plateau at the top, so most of the domain is flat. The right surface is the Tsallis SoftArgmax with Tsallis regularization. It curves smoothly from purple to yellow with a visible slope across the domain and no large flat region far from the optimum. Both use the viridis colormap and have a projected contour shadow on the floor. The eye goes first to the sharp cliff on the left, then to the smooth sweep on the right.
caption: Regularized value landscapes (with temperature λ = 1) for a onestate, two-action MDP: softmax with entropy (left) versus α-Tsallis SoftArgmax with α-Tsallis regularization (right, α = 0.1). The value of the classical coupling Entropy–Softmax is much flatter than for our proposed coupling Tsallis– Tsallis. Using the latter removes flat areas that are far from the solution, allowing policy gradient methods to escape the gravitational pull.
abstract: Policy gradient methods are known to be highly sensitive to the choice of policy parameterization. In particular, the widely used softmax parameterization can induce ill-conditioned optimization landscapes and lead to exponentially slow convergence. Although this can be mitigated by preconditioning, this solution is often computationally expensive. Instead, we propose replacing the softmax with an alternative family of policy parameterizations based on the generalized f-softargmax. We further advocate coupling this parameterization with a regularizer induced by the same f-divergence, which improves the optimization landscape and ensures that the resulting regularized objective satisfies a Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality. Leveraging this structure, we establish the first explicit non-asymptotic last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic policy gradient methods for finite MDPs without any form of preconditioning. We also derive sample-complexity bounds for the unregularized problem and show that f-PG, with Tsallis divergences achieves polynomial sample complexity in contrast to the exponential complexity incurred by the standard softmax parameterization.
